item.description:
We tested Nemotron 3 Ultra on agentic chip design.
The task is RTL coding: a model iteratively writes the code that defines a chip's logic, runs it through a simulator, reads the failures, and rewrites.
Across nine categories of real design work, Nemotron 3 Ultra averaged a 97.1% pass rate at 6,629 tokens per iteration, best of the open models tested on both.
item.author: NVIDIA AI

Yes, open-source / open-weight models are important for a healthy AI ecosystem. That's how we can verify things, check claims, and keep up outside the closed labs. Plus, it gives us the freedom to run AI on our own hardware if we are not ready to share personal data and IPs with closed labs through using their models. (Not that proprietary models are bad, actually I use them a lot as well, but it wouldn't healthy not to have any alternatives.)

item.title: The Fastest Way Into AI Engineering if You Already Have a Job
item.description: If you're already employed, the fastest path into AI engineering is to become the AI person on your team. Volunteer to build the AI feature nobody else wants to own. Ship one thing with AI inside your current company. An internal transfer to an AI or AI-adjacent role is almost always easier than landing one completely from scratch. So if you can learn inside your company, even if it isn't your main role, you build real use cases and experience you can point back to later, and that makes everything easier. I've seen this work firsthand helping developers land these jobs. #techwithtim #aienginee

item.title: How to Get the Most Out of Fable 5 and GPT 5.6 Sol
item.description: Fable 5 and GPT‑5.6 Sol require new prompting patterns: explicit boundaries, iterative steering, and matching compute and effort to the task. Best practices include deleting repeated instructions, giving concrete directives, using voice dictation for richer context, and setting measurable quality bars. Higher-impact use comes from onboarding models with deep context, treating unknowns as collaboration points, and running automated loops until success criteria are met. item.title: Literally everyone hated this feature
item.description: Did Meta actually think we wouldn’t notice this? 🫣 Recently, Meta rolled out a new image-generation feature called Muse Image. On paper, it was pitched as a creative new AI tool. In reality, it turned into a massive privacy and safety concern overnight. By default, the feature automatically opted in public accounts, allowing anyone to simply @ a handle and use Meta AI to generate entirely new images using that person's likeness with NO permission required.
